title: F90 SELECT CASE — supports ranges, multiple values, and CASE DEFAULT
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE GRADE_FROM_SCORE(SCORE, GRADE)
C     SELECT CASE with ranges (CASE (90:)), value lists
C     (CASE (60, 70)), and a CASE DEFAULT for unmatched values.
C     Java's switch has none of these; Java's enhanced switch (14+)
C     supports ranges via 'when' clauses but earlier targets need
C     a chain of if-else. Pattern faithful translation is
C     non-trivial.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER SCORE
      CHARACTER*1 GRADE
      SELECT CASE (SCORE)
         CASE (90:)
            GRADE = 'A'
         CASE (80:89)
            GRADE = 'B'
         CASE (70:79)
            GRADE = 'C'
         CASE (60:69)
            GRADE = 'D'
         CASE DEFAULT
            GRADE = 'F'
      END SELECT
      END
notes: SELECT CASE is straightforward to port but worth surfacing because (a) the open-ended range CASE (90:) covers any score >= 90 including 1_000_000, which might not be the caller's intent, and (b) negative scores fall to CASE DEFAULT silently. Each is a candidate open question.
